title: ZCC end-user support options (App Supportability)
aliases: end user ticket submission to zscaler

prose.text: The App Supportability settings decide what users can do for themselves when Client Connector misbehaves, and what an admin can collect without them. Most of the mechanics live in the logging, password and app profile subjects linked below.

{{entry-points}} {{routing}} {{requires-support-access}} {{report-an-issue-visibility}} What the form sends and who can read the logs: [[zcc.logging.collection:report-an-issue]], [[zcc.logging.collection:support-settings]], [[zcc.logging.collection:only-zscaler-decrypts]].

What the log bundle contains is open {{gap:bundle-contents}}. Whether user submissions leave an audit trail is open {{gap:submission-audit}}; what the console audit log records for admins is in [[zcc.audit-logs]].

{{user-log-controls}} The overview words the export as a text file, against a ZIP file elsewhere [[zcc.end-user:export-logs-format]]. {{app-logs-option}} The fetch itself: [[zcc.logging.collection:fetch-prereq]], [[zcc.logging.collection:fetch-scope]]. Hide Logging Control and what users can do with logs: [[zcc.logging.user-access:hidden-blocks]], [[zcc.logging.user-access:export-encryption]].

{{telemetry}} {{telemetry-tenant-switch}} {{telemetry-app-profile}} What it collects beyond the app profile's metric list, and whether the tenant switch reaches iOS profiles, are not stated {{gap:telemetry-scope}}.

Restart Service and Repair App: [[zcc.support-options.restart-and-repair]]. Passwords on logout, disable, exit and uninstall: [[zcc.passwords-and-otp]]. Anti-tampering and its OTP reactivation timer: [[zcc.app-profiles.advanced-settings:anti-tampering]]; the install parameter: [[zcc.install.precedence:anti-tampering]]. Users' reasons for disabling a service: [[zcc.app-profiles.advanced-settings:send-disable-reason]], exported as in [[zcc.devices.exports]].

Whether a per-service disable password gates only its own service is open {{gap:per-service-independence}}. Whether anti-tampering constrains Citrix VDI deployments is open {{gap:anti-tampering-vdi}}.

prose.heading: Sign-in settings and the command line

prose.text: IdP username autofill, automatic Private Access reauthentication and registering devices with the ZPA IdP username: [[zcc.support-options.authentication]]. The command line (ZSACli and zscli): [[zcc.support-options.cli]].

{{field-ui-mapping}} The read, the Go-only write and the field encodings: [[zcc.api.company-wire]]. What a new tenant starts with is open {{gap:toggle-defaults}}, and so is when a change reaches enrolled devices {{gap:tenant-setting-propagation}}.
Telemetry collection and non-admin access to local log files are User Privacy settings: [[zcc.web-privacy.collection]].

page-settings.statement: The App Supportability page (Infrastructure > Advanced Settings > App Supportability) configures user access to logging controls, to support options and to the restart and repair options; Client Connector Telemetry; automatic username population for IdP authentication; automatic ZPA reauthentication; and registering devices with the ZPA IdP username.

quotes: On the App Supportability page (Infrastructure > Advanced Settings > App Supportability):
Configure user access to logging controls for Zscaler Client Connector.
Configure user access to support options for Zscaler Client Connector.
Configure user access to the restart and repair options for Zscaler Client Connector.
Configure Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry.
Configure automatic username population for IdP authentication.
Configure automatic ZPA reauthentication.
Register devices with the ZPA IdP username.

user-log-controls.statement: The App Supportability overview says users given access to logging controls can export logs as a text file, clear logs and change the logging mode, and that a support request can go only to the organization's support admin or also directly to Zscaler Support.

quotes: Allow users to access logging controls. Users can export logs as a text file, clear logs, and change the logging mode.
You can specify whether their request goes only to your organization's support admin or whether it also goes directly to Zscaler Support.

telemetry.statement: Client Connector Telemetry gets telemetry and device event information from devices, collecting a subset of the information Digital Experience (ZDX) already collects; it also enables device event collection, which provides reporting such as the Device Events page and the Failed Posture Devices page.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry gets telemetry and device event information from devices.
It collects a subset of the information already collected by Digital Experience (ZDX).
It also enables device event collection, which provides valuable reporting such as the Device Events page and the Failed Posture Devices page.

telemetry-tenant-switch.statement: Enabling or disabling Client Connector Telemetry for all users is a tenant setting whose default value is enabled. When enabled, the Telemetry option on all existing and new app profiles for Windows, macOS, Android and Linux is enabled and can be disabled per profile; when disabled, the option on all existing app profiles is also disabled and cannot be enabled.

quotes: You can use this setting to enable or disable Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry for all users. The default value is enabled.

When the option is enabled, the Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry option on all existing and new app profiles for Windows, macOS, Android, and Linux is enabled, but if required, you can disable the option on individual app profiles.
If you disable the option, the Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry option on all existing app profiles is also disabled, and you cannot enable it.

telemetry-app-profile.statement: On the app profile, the Telemetry settings are available only on Client Connector 4.6 and later for Windows and 4.5.1 and later for macOS and are disabled if the tenant-wide option is disabled; the profile's Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry collects metrics including device events, statistics, profile, statistics for Client Connector processes and the top 5 processes, which the page says include no personally identifiable information, and its default value is enabled.

quotes: On the App Supportability tab, select Enable Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry.
This feature is available only for Zscaler Client Connector version 4.6 and later for Windows. If the Enable Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry option is disabled, this option is disabled.
This feature is available only for Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5.1 and later for macOS. If the Enable Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry option is disabled, this option is disabled.

evidence.after: This feature is available only for Zscaler Client Connector version 4.6 and later for Windows. If the Enable Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry option is disabled, this option is disabled.
quotes: Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry: Enable to collect metrics including device events, statistics, profile, statistics for Zscaler Client Connector processes, and the top 5 processes. These metrics do not include personally identifiable information (PII). The default value is enabled.

report-an-issue-visibility.statement: The Report an Issue option appears in the app user interface only if the IT admin has enabled it in the Client Connector support configuration. On submitting the form, depending on the organization's setup, the app might send an email to the organization's support admin or submit a ticket directly to Zscaler Support, of which the support admin receives a copy, and the user receives an email acknowledging the support request.

quotes: The Report an Issue option appears in the app user interface only if your IT admin has enabled it in your Zscaler Client Connector support configuration.

When you submit the form, depending on your organization's setup, Zscaler Client Connector might send an email to your organization's support admin or submit a ticket directly to Zscaler Support (your support admin receives a copy of this ticket as well).
After you submit the form, you receive an email acknowledging the support request.

entry-points.statement: Users reach the support options by clicking Report an Issue in Client Connector's More window or from its system tray icon.

quotes: Your users can access these support options by clicking Report an Issue from the More window of Zscaler Client Connector or the Zscaler Client Connector system tray icon.

routing.statement: Support requests go either to the organization's support admin only, or to both the support admin and Zscaler Support.

quotes: You can configure support requests to go only to your organization’s support admin or go to both the support admin and Zscaler Support.

requires-support-access.statement: Admin Email Address to Send Logs and Enable End User Ticket Submission to Zscaler both apply only when support access is enabled.

quotes: Admin Email Address to Send Logs: If you enabled support access, enter the email address of your organization's designated support admin or team.

Enable End User Ticket Submission to Zscaler: If you enabled support access, select this option if you also want a ticket to be automatically sent to Zscaler Support when the user chooses Report an Issue.

app-logs-option.statement: The App Supportability option Client Connector App Logs is what allows collecting Client Connector logs per enrolled device, through Fetch Logs on the device's details.

quotes: Client Connector App Logs: Allows users to collect Client Connector logs per enrolled device. To fetch logs, go to Enrolled Devices. On the Device Details tab, click Fetch Logs.

field-ui-mapping.statement: By name, the company-info fields `supportEnabled`, `supportAdminEmail`, `supportTicketEnabled`, `disableLoggingControls` and `fetchLogsForAdminsEnabled` hold Enable Support Access, Admin Email Address to Send Logs, Enable End User Ticket Submission to Zscaler, Hide Logging Control and Client Connector App Logs.
field-ui-mapping.conditions: Matched by name between the company-info fields and the App Supportability options; no source states the mapping.

quotes: SupportAdminEmail string `json:"supportAdminEmail"`
SupportEnabled int `json:"supportEnabled"`
FetchLogsForAdminsEnabled int `json:"fetchLogsForAdminsEnabled"`
SupportTicketEnabled int `json:"supportTicketEnabled"`
DisableLoggingControls int `json:"disableLoggingControls"`

telemetry-scope.title: What Telemetry collects beyond the app profile's metric list, and whether the tenant switch reaches iOS profiles
telemetry-scope.detail: The tenant page says Telemetry collects a subset of what ZDX collects and names Windows, macOS, Android and Linux app profiles; the app profile capture lists its metrics and gives versions for Windows and macOS only. Whether iOS profiles are affected is not stated.

bundle-contents.title: What the Report an Issue log bundle contains
bundle-contents.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the bundle holds client operational logs, service logs and system metadata, and may include connection metadata (destination IPs, ports, hostnames), user identity (username, tenant domain), device identifiers (UDID, hostname) and activity timestamps; it is stored nowhere but the email and the ticket. Partly answered since: when Client Connector collects traceroute information, the traceroute log files are included when a user reports an issue or exports logs ([[zcc.logging.collection:traceroute-in-logs]]). File names, rotation, size limits and PII content are not documented. Former zcc-65 asked also which files the Export Logs ZIP holds, and whether either archive carries OS network configuration, driver information or other artifacts beyond Client Connector's own logs. Former zcc-37 asked whether Client Connector stages the bundle in a predictable local directory before uploading it, which matters to DLP controls that scan outbound email attachments.
bundle-contents.blocks: privacy and data-residency reviews of sending bundles to Zscaler Support

submission-audit.title: Whether Report an Issue submissions and user log exports are auditable
submission-audit.detail: Unverified legacy statement: no audit trail exists for user-invoked support actions, and the disable-reasons export is the closest admin-side signal. No source describes an audit record either way. Former zcc-38 asked specifically whether the ZCC portal's audit log records the time, device and user of a Report an Issue submission, separately from the email delivery receipt.
submission-audit.blocks: investigations that need to know when a user submitted or exported logs

toggle-defaults.title: The App Supportability settings' values on a new tenant
toggle-defaults.detail: Partly settled: the Telemetry tenant setting's default value is enabled (telemetry-tenant-switch). Still open for the rest. Unverified legacy statement: support access, ticket submission, Hide Logging Control and admin log fetch are off on a new tenant, the admin email is empty, and app profiles set no password gate. The help article describes the options without defaults, and the SDK models declare the fields without default values.
toggle-defaults.blocks: telling a tenant's deliberate choice from an untouched default in posture or hygiene reviews

tenant-setting-propagation.title: When App Supportability changes reach enrolled devices
tenant-setting-propagation.detail: Unverified legacy statement: App Supportability settings, app profile password gates and web privacy flags reach enrolled devices at the next Client Connector restart or user logout and login, with no real-time push. The vendor states this only for app profiles; these settings are tenant-wide, not part of the app profile.
tenant-setting-propagation.blocks: telling an admin when a support setting change takes effect on devices

per-service-independence.title: Whether per-service disable passwords gate only their own service
per-service-independence.detail: Unverified legacy statement: per-product disable passwords (ZIA, ZPA, ZDX, ZDP, ZAD) are independent of the whole-agent disable password, so a user with only a ZIA disable password set must enter it only to disable ZIA, not ZPA or the agent. The vendor describes each password's own action but not their interaction.
per-service-independence.blocks: predicting which user actions a partial password set still allows

anti-tampering-vdi.title: Whether anti-tampering interacts with Citrix VDI settings
anti-tampering-vdi.detail: Unverified legacy statement: on Windows with Citrix VDI, ENABLEANTITAMPERING interacts with HIDEAPPUIONLAUNCH, and anti-tampering in VDI should be tested before rollout. The vendor ties hideAppUIOnLaunch for non-persistent Citrix VDIs to strict enforcement (zcc.install.strict-enforcement:citrix-hide-ui), not to anti-tampering.
